# Data quality failures

<small>Source: [`R/errors-quality.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/r-dataexcept/blob/main/R/errors-quality.R) · Help: `?data_quality_errors`</small>

Errors about the data itself rather than the code handling it: a file in
the wrong format, a schema that does not match, drift from a reference
distribution, leakage between training and test data, classes too
imbalanced to learn from, and outlier detection that could not run. All
inherit from `dataexcept_data_science_error`.

## Usage

```r
data_format_error(expected_formats, found_format, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

schema_mismatch_error(expected, found, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

data_drift_error(
  feature,
  drift_score,
  message = NULL,
  parent = NULL,
  call = NULL
)

data_leakage_error(feature, stage, message = NULL, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

data_imbalance_error(
  ratio,
  threshold,
  message = NULL,
  parent = NULL,
  call = NULL
)

outlier_detection_error(method, details = NULL, parent = NULL, call = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`expected_formats`
:   Character vector of the formats accepted, such as
    `c("csv", "parquet")`.

`found_format`
:   The format found.

`parent`
:   The condition that caused this one, or `NULL`.

`call`
:   The call to report, or `NULL`.

`expected`, `found`
:   Descriptions of the schema expected and the schema
    found, each a single string.

`feature`
:   Name of the feature concerned.

`drift_score`
:   The drift statistic, written to four decimal places in
    the default message.

`message`
:   A message to use instead of the default.

`stage`
:   The stage at which the leak was found, such as
    `"cross-validation"`.

`ratio`
:   The ratio of the smallest class to the largest.

`threshold`
:   The smallest ratio accepted.

`method`
:   The name of the detection method.

`details`
:   Optional detail, appended to the message.

## Value

A condition inheriting from `dataexcept_data_science_error`.

## Details

Their failure metadata is `"unknown"` by default: the same data would fail
again, but whether the data will change is for the caller to say.

## Examples

```r
check_balance <- function(y, threshold = 0.2) {
  counts <- table(y)
  ratio <- min(counts) / max(counts)
  if (ratio < threshold) stop(data_imbalance_error(ratio, threshold))
  invisible(y)
}
tryCatch(
  check_balance(c(rep("no", 95), rep("yes", 5))),
  dataexcept_data_imbalance_error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

err <- data_drift_error("income", drift_score = 0.4172)
err$drift_score

schema_mismatch_error(
  expected = "id: integer, amount: numeric",
  found = "id: integer, amount: character"
)
```
